YOUR FIRST DAYS IN GERMANY
Welcome to Your New Beginning
Congratulations!
You have successfully completed the visa process and arrived in Germany. Starting a
new life in another country is a major achievement, and it is completely normal to feel
excited, nervous or even a little uncertain during your ﬁrst days.
Remember that every international driver experiences a "ﬁrst day. " You are not expected
to know everything immediately. Give yourself time to learn and adapt.

Your Arrival
After arriving in Germany, your employer or a designated company representative will
normally welcome you and help you with the ﬁrst important steps.
Depending on the employer, this may include:
✔ Transportation from the airport, train station or meeting point
✔ Accommodation or temporary housing
✔ Introduction to your workplace
✔ Meeting your colleagues and supervisors
✔ Information about your daily work routine
Every company is different, so the exact procedure may vary.

Accommodation
Many employers assist international drivers in ﬁnding suitable accommodation,
especially during the ﬁrst weeks after arrival.
Your accommodation may be:
• A company apartment
• Shared accommodation with other employees
• Temporary housing until permanent accommodation is arranged
Always keep your accommodation clean, respect your neighbours and follow the house
rules.
Good behaviour creates a positive ﬁrst impression.

Registration and Administrative Procedures
During your ﬁrst days, several administrative tasks may need to be completed.
Depending on your individual situation, these may include:
• Registration of your residence
• Health insurance
• Opening a bank account
• Tax identiﬁcation procedures
• Other employment-related formalities
Your employer or EuroJobsCenter will explain which steps apply to your situation.

Getting to Know Your Employer
During your ﬁrst days, you will become familiar with your employer, your workplace and
your responsibilities.
You may receive information about:
• Company policies
• Safety regulations
• Working hours
• Driving schedules
• Company vehicles
• Communication procedures
Do not hesitate to ask questions if anything is unclear.
Every employer expects new employees to learn during the ﬁrst days.

Practical Driving Assessment
Many employers perform a practical driving assessment before assigning a vehicle.
This is a normal procedure and is designed to ensure the safety of both the driver and
the company.
The assessment may include:
• Vehicle inspection
• Coupling and uncoupling trailers (if applicable)
• Reversing
• Parking
• Safe driving
• Use of company equipment
Do not be nervous.
The purpose of the assessment is to understand your current driving skills and, where
necessary, provide additional guidance or training.

Communication Is Important
Good communication is one of the keys to success.
If you do not understand something, ask.
If you make a mistake, be honest.
If you have a problem, inform your employer immediately.
Professional communication builds trust and helps avoid misunderstandings.

Your First Impression Matters
Your ﬁrst days create the ﬁrst impression.
Simple things make a big difference:
✔ Be punctual.
✔ Be respectful.
✔ Listen carefully.
✔ Follow instructions.
✔ Drive safely.
✔ Treat company property with care.
✔ Be willing to learn.
Employers appreciate drivers who show a positive attitude and a strong work ethic.

Remember
Your ﬁrst week is not about being perfect.
It is about learning, adapting and becoming part of your new team.
Thousands of international professional truck drivers have successfully started their
careers in Germany.
With patience, professionalism and a positive attitude, you can do the same.
Welcome to Germany, and we wish you every success in your new career.
